title: The Friday Shipment
brief: It is Friday at 3 p.m. at Meridian Works. A batch of 400 shafts for a key customer must leave at 5 p.m. to meet the contract date. Final inspection found 1 diameter reading at the upper limit and 1 just above it. The supervisor proposes shipping now and "sorting it out on Monday". You have 12 visit points to gather what you need and make a decision you can justify.

actions.label: Inspection record for the shaft batch
Inspector: how the readings were taken
General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: Supervisor: who can approve a concession
A staff member: anything else to mention
actions.note: The staff member has nothing further to add on this topic.

actions.label: Older records for this area
actions.note: The older records show nothing relevant to this visit.

actions.label: Notices and signs in the area
actions.note: The notices are current and not relevant to this visit.

evidence.text: Inspection record for batch S-902: sample of 32 shafts; 1 reading at 25.020 mm (limit 25.020) and 1 at 25.023 mm. The batch status is "released" in the system.
evidence.whyItMatters: When a nonconforming output is found, the batch must be held until a disposition is authorized. A release status contradicts the result.
evidence.missedExplanation: Compare the measured values with the limit and the batch status.

evidence.text: Inspector: "I measured both twice with M-14 and got the same result." The repeat readings are recorded.
evidence.whyItMatters: The result is repeatable and recorded; it can be relied on.
evidence.missedExplanation: Conforming evidence: the data is sound.
evidence.falseFindingNote: Careful repeat measurement is good practice.

evidence.text: Supervisor: "Two parts out of 400 is nothing. The customer will never notice and we'll lose the contract if we're late." No release authority is cited. (note 2)
evidence.whyItMatters: Release with open nonconformities needs an authorized decision, and, where applicable, the customer's agreement. Schedule pressure does not change that.
evidence.missedExplanation: Listen for pressure that replaces authorization.

evidence.text: Supervisor: "The quality manager or deputy can approve concessions. Both are on site until 6 p.m."
evidence.whyItMatters: Authority for concessions is defined and available in time.
evidence.missedExplanation: Conforming evidence that shows a lawful route exists.
evidence.falseFindingNote: The roles are defined and reachable. Conforming.

evidence.text: Concession procedure QP-12 requires an authorized approver and, where the contract says so, customer agreement before shipment.
evidence.whyItMatters: The organization has a process for this exact situation.
evidence.falseFindingNote: The procedure is sound. The risk is in bypassing it.

evidence.text: Customer agreement CA-7 requires written customer approval before shipping any part outside drawing limits. No request has been sent.
evidence.whyItMatters: Customer requirements that apply to deviations must be met.
evidence.missedExplanation: Read the customer agreement for deviation terms.

evidence.text: Micrometer M-14 is calibrated, due in 3 months.
Machine log shows the tool offset was adjusted by 0.01 mm at part 260 with no note of why.
evidence.whyItMatters: Recording why an adjustment was made helps scope a problem. The adjustment may explain the high readings.
evidence.missedExplanation: Machine logs can show when a shift started.

evidence.text: Carrier booking can be moved to Saturday 10 a.m. at extra cost; the contract date is Monday.
evidence.whyItMatters: There is time to decide properly. The schedule is less fixed than stated.
evidence.missedExplanation: Check how firm a deadline really is.

evidence.text: The shift handover board lists "S-902 ship 5 p.m." in large letters.
evidence.whyItMatters: A plan on a board is communication, not a nonconformity.
evidence.falseFindingNote: The board shows the plan. It is not evidence of a breach.

evidence.text: The shipping paperwork template is revision 6, which is current.

decisions.prompt: What do you do at 3:15 p.m.?
options: Agree to ship and note it for Monday
Ask for the batch to be held, raise the matter with the quality manager now, and propose a quick 100 percent diameter sort with a customer deviation request if any parts remain outside limits
Say nothing; it is the supervisor's call
decisions.rationale: Holding and escalating uses the defined route. A sort may let most parts ship on time, and the customer decides on any deviation. Speaking up is part of the investigator's role.
optionFeedback: This ships a known nonconformity without authority or customer approval.
This is proportionate, uses the defined authority, and keeps the delivery possible.
Staying silent leaves a known issue unaddressed.
Scrapping is disproportionate when sorting can separate good parts.

decisions.prompt: How should the supervisor's concern about the contract be handled?
options: Acknowledge it and show the options: a Saturday carrier slot and a sort, so the customer receives conforming parts by the contract date
Promise the customer the parts are fine
decisions.rationale: Pressure is real. A good response addresses the business need through the system, without blame.

containment: Hold batch S-902 and change its system status from released to on hold
correction: Sort all 400 shafts; separate any outside limits and request customer deviation or rework as authorized
cause: The system allowed release with an open nonconformity, and the tool offset change was not recorded with a reason
corrective: Block release in the system while a nonconformity is open; require a reason for every offset adjustment
effectiveness: Check for a quarter that no batch is released with an open nonconformity record

debriefText.found: You held the line on release while offering a route that meets the date.
debriefText.missed: Under pressure, check two things first: who has authority, and what the customer agreement says.
debriefText.falseFinding: A plan on a board and current paperwork are not problems.
